Copernicus dies in Frombork; De revolutionibus is published that year.

Title: Copernicus' heliocentric model
Body-Text: In his landmark 1543 treatise De revolutionis orbium coelestium, Polish astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus challenged the geocentric theory, starting what would be an astonomical discovery (get it?) by placing the Sun at the heart of the solar system. He also proposed that Earth rotates daily on its axis and orbits the sun annually alongside the other planets. This bold assumption naturally explained retrograde motion as an optical illusion caused by Earth overtaking outer planets.
